raw_case_text:
In July 2005, a 33 year old Zimbabwean female, resident in the UK for 8 years, was admitted with a week history of fever, headache, and neck stiffness. She had no past medical history of note. Systemic examination showed fever and meningism but no focal neurological deficits. Blood tests revealed mild anaemia, lymphopenia, and raised C-reactive protein. An HIV test was positive with CD4 count of 51 cells/muL (4%). CT head without contrast showed marked meningeal inflammation but no focal lesions. A lumbar puncture (LP) revealed raised opening pressure (OP) of 27 cms H20, lymphocyte count (30/cu mm), protein (1.33 g/L), and CSF: serum glucose ratio of 50%. Cerebral spinal fluid (CSF) microscopy showed multiple yeast with high cryptococcal antigen (CRAG) titre of >1 : 25,600. CSF Acid-alcohol fast bacilli (AAFB), toxoplasmosis, and viral screens were negative. The patient was started on standard amphotericin with flucytosine and prophylactic cotrimoxazole.
On day five of therapy, she began to complain of increasing headache and neck stiffness. A right-sided sixth nerve palsy was noted as a new neurological sign. An MRI brain showed changes in keeping with chronic meningitis and occipitoparietal changes (Figure 1(a)). Repeat LP revealed OP of 40 cms H20 with persistently high protein and lymphocyte count. Over the next two weeks, the patient required a lumbar drain to alleviate excruciating pressure-related headaches.
CSF cultures revealed Cryptococcus neoformans sensitive to amphotericin B (Minimum Inhibitory Concentration "MIC" 0.125 mg/L) and itraconazole (MIC 0.03 mg/L) and intermediate to fluconazole (MIC 4.0 mg/L) and flucytosine (MIC 8.0 mgL). Amphotericin and flucytosine were continued for four weeks and then switched to oral fluconazole 800 mg once daily. This prolonged initial phase was based on symptom severity, high fungal burden, and relatively high MIC to fluconazole. A repeat MRI head showed regression of the previous changes.
Four weeks into cryptococcal treatment, combined antiretroviral therapy (cART) was initiated with Kivexa (abacavir and lamivudine) and efavirenz. The patient then developed a new, persistent headache and subsequent LPs showed raised OPs, lymphocytes, and protein. Yeast cells persisted in CSF for 3 months after starting amphotericin and flucytosine and CSF cultures remained positive until September 2005 (2 months after treatment start).
By October 2005, CSF cultures were negative for Cryptococcus and the patient had improved clinically. VL was undetectable and CD4 counts had risen minimally from 51 (4%) to 67 cells/muL (6%). She was discharged home on fluconazole (800 mg OD), cotrimoxazole, and cART.
The patient then went on to have a difficult clinical course with recurrent admissions over the subsequent 14 months (Table 1).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 33-year-old Zimbabwean female presented with a 1-week history of fever, headache, and neck stiffness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient, who had resided in the UK for 8 years with no prior medical history, presented in July 2005 with 1 week of fever, severe headache, and neck stiffness.
subjective.past_medical_history: No prior medical history of note; originally from Zimbabwe, resident in the UK for 8 years.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, headache, and neck stiffness (and subsequent diplopia/sixth nerve palsy on day 5).

objective.physical_examination: Fever and meningismus without focal neurological deficits on admission; on day 5 of therapy, developed worsening neck stiffness and a new right-sided sixth cranial nerve palsy.
objective.routine_investigations: Mild anemia, lymphopenia, elevated C-reactive protein, and positive HIV test.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-cell count was 51 cells/uL (4%). Non-contrast head CT showed marked meningeal inflammation without focal lesions; day 5 brain MRI showed chronic meningitis and occipitoparietal changes. Initial lumbar puncture showed opening pressure (OP) 27 cmH2O (rising to 40 cmH2O on day 5), lymphocytes 30/mm3, protein 1.33 g/L, CSF:serum glucose ratio 50%, multiple yeasts on microscopy, CSF cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) titer >1:25,600, and negative CSF AFB, toxoplasmosis, and viral screens.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis of HIV/AIDS-associated Cryptococcus neoformans meningitis complicated by severe intracranial hypertension and subsequent relapsing immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS), confirmed by CSF microscopy, CSF CrAg titer >1:25,600, and CSF fungal culture isolating C. neoformans (MICs: amphotericin B 0.125 mg/L, itraconazole 0.03 mg/L, fluconazole 4.0 mg/L, flucytosine 8.0 mg/L). Treated with 4 weeks of induction amphotericin B plus flucytosine, a 2-week lumbar drain for severe intracranial hypertension (OP 40 cmH2O), prophylactic cotrimoxazole, and consolidation oral fluconazole 800 mg daily. Initiation of cART (abacavir/lamivudine and efavirenz) at week 4 triggered persistent headaches and elevated OPs; CSF cultures sterilized by October 2005 (with undetectable HIV VL and CD4 67 cells/uL), though she experienced recurrent admissions over the next 14 months.
